sections.content: How many people are "catering and bar managers"?

67,755 people

were counted on the census as "catering and bar managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Catering and bar managers co-ordinate the catering and bar facilities and services of licensed premises, factories, shops, theatres, educational premises and other establishments.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "catering and bar managers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "catering and bar managers", 13.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "catering and bar managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "catering and bar managers" included:

  • sales administrators
  • financial administrative occupations (other)
  • road construction operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "catering and bar managers" there were more women than men (56.2% compared with 43.8%).

This means "catering and bar managers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 43.8% and women made up 56.2% of "catering and bar managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "catering and bar managers" included:

  • financial accounts managers
  • further education teaching professionals
  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "catering and bar managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "catering and bar managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "catering and bar managers", 10% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (65.4% compared with 34.6%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.1%) than self-employed (11.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
